subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure of a closed ball of an n-plane: H^n(T ∩ B_r(0)) = ω_n r^n
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, T ∈ G(N,n) (T : Grassmannian N n, with n-dimensional linear subspace T.plane ⊆ ℝ^N = Euclidean N) and r ∈ ℝ with r ≥ 0. Then μHE[n](T.plane ∩ closedBall 0 r) = unitBallVolume n · ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n in [0, ∞], i.e. H^n(T ∩ B_r(0)) = ω_n r^n, where H^n = μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N, B_r(0) is the closed ball and ω_n = unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (T : Grassmannian N n) (r : ℝ), 0 ≤ r → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) ((T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)) ∩ closedBall 0 r) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal r ^ n
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5 (plane balls) of the parent proof, made self-contained.

Notation: P := T.plane, a linear subspace of ℝ^N = Euclidean N; |·| is the Euclidean norm; ℝ^n := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n); B_ρ(0) is the closed ball of radius ρ about 0 in the indicated space.

1. Orthonormal basis indexed by Fin n. finrank_ℝ P = n (Grassmannian.finrank_plane). Hence the standard orthonormal basis of P (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ P, indexed by Fin (finrank ℝ P)) reindexed along finCongr T.finrank_plane is an orthonormal basis b of P indexed by Fin n. Its coordinate map b.repr : P ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ^n is a linear isometry equivalence; put e := b.repr.symm : ℝ^n ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] P.

2. Isometric parametrisation of P. Let ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^N, ι(v) := (e v : ℝ^N), the composite of e with the inclusion P ↪ ℝ^N (in Lean: J := T.plane.subtypeₗᵢ.comp b.repr.symm.toLinearIsometry, a linear isometry ℝ^n →ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ^N). Then ι is an isometry, |ι(v)| = |v| and ι(v) ∈ P for every v ∈ ℝ^n.

3. ι(B_r(0)) = P ∩ B_r(0), with B_r(0) ⊆ ℝ^n on the left and ⊆ ℝ^N on the right. (⊆) If |v| ≤ r then ι(v) ∈ P and |ι(v)| = |v| ≤ r. (⊇) If w ∈ P and |w| ≤ r, put v := b.repr ⟨w, w ∈ P⟩ = e⁻¹(w) ∈ ℝ^n; then ι(v) = e(e⁻¹ w) = w, and |v| = |⟨w, _⟩| = |w| ≤ r because b.repr preserves norms and the norm of P is the restriction of the norm of ℝ^N.

4. Transfer to ℝ^n. ι is an isometry between metric spaces carrying their Borel σ-algebras, so μHE[n](ι(E)) = μHE[n](E) for every E ⊆ ℝ^n (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and on ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) one has μHE[n] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). By 3, μHE[n](P ∩ B_r(0)) = μHE[n](ι(B_r(0))) = volume(B_r(0)).

5. Volume of a ball in ℝ^n. volume on ℝ^n is an additive Haar measure and finrank_ℝ ℝ^n = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), so, as r ≥ 0, volume(B_r(0)) = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) · volume(ball (0 : ℝ^n) 1) (Measure.addHaar_closedBall). Since r ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) = ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n (ENNReal.ofReal_pow), and volume(ball (0 : ℝ^n) 1) = unitBallVolume n by definition. Hence volume(B_r(0)) = ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n · unitBallVolume n = unitBallVolume n · ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n by commutativity of multiplication in [0, ∞].

6. Combining 4 and 5, μHE[n](T.plane ∩ closedBall 0 r) = unitBallVolume n · ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n. The argument is uniform in n, including n = 0 (ℝ^0 is a point, r^0 = 1, and both sides equal unitBallVolume 0 = 1), so no case distinction is needed. ∎
proof_key_steps: finrank T.plane = n, so reindexing stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T.plane along finCongr T.finrank_plane gives an orthonormal basis b indexed by Fin n
ι := T.plane.subtypeₗᵢ ∘ b.repr.symm is a linear isometry ℝ^n → ℝ^N with values in T.plane and |ι v| = |v|
T.plane ∩ B_r(0) = ι(B_r(0))
μHE[n](ι E) = μHE[n](E) = volume E on ℝ^n (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume)
volume(B_r(0)) = ofReal(r^n)·volume(ball 0 1) = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(r)^n (Measure.addHaar_closedBall, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, ENNReal.ofReal_pow)

subproblems.title: Plane integrals of the radial cut-offs: ω_n(1−κ)^n ≤ ∫_T χ_{1−κ,1} dH^n and ∫_T χ_{1,1+κ} dH^n ≤ ω_n(1+κ)^n
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, T ∈ G(N,n) (Grassmannian N n) and κ ∈ ℝ with 0 < κ < 1. Let H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^N = Euclidean N and ω_n = (unitBallVolume n).toReal, and for y ∈ ℝ^N let χ⁻(y) = max(0, min(1, (1 − |y|)/κ)) and χ⁺(y) = max(0, min(1, (1 + κ − |y|)/κ)) (the cut-offs χ_{1−κ,1} and χ_{1,1+κ} of the parent proof, χ_{a,b}(y) = max(0, min(1, (b − |y|)/(b − a)))). Then ω_n(1 − κ)^n ≤ ∫_{T.plane} χ⁻ dH^n and ∫_{T.plane} χ⁺ dH^n ≤ ω_n(1 + κ)^n, the integrals being real Bochner integrals with respect to H^n restricted to T.plane.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (T : Grassmannian N n) (κ : ℝ), 0 < κ → κ < 1 → (unitBallVolume n).toReal * (1 - κ) ^ n ≤ ∫ y in (T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), max 0 (min 1 ((1 - ‖y‖) / κ)) ∂μHE[n] ∧ ∫ y in (T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), max 0 (min 1 ((1 + κ - ‖y‖) / κ)) ∂μHE[n] ≤ (unitBallVolume n).toReal * (1 + κ) ^ n
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 6 (plane integrals) of the parent proof, with the cut-off facts of its Step 3; it uses only the sibling plane_ball (Submission.frt_vgm_tba_plane_closedBall_hausdorff).

Notation: μ := H^n ⌞ T.plane = μHE[n].restrict T.plane, so ∫_{T.plane} f dH^n = ∫ f dμ for every f : ℝ^N → ℝ. B_r(0) is the closed ball in ℝ^N. For a ∈ ℝ let χ_a(y) := max(0, min(1, (a − |y|)/κ)); thus χ⁻ = χ_1 and χ⁺ = χ_{1+κ}.

1. Balls. Let r ≥ 0. B_r(0) is closed, hence Borel, so μ(B_r(0)) = H^n(B_r(0) ∩ T.plane) (Measure.restrict_apply) = H^n(T.plane ∩ B_r(0)) = unitBallVolume n · ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n by the sibling plane_ball, i.e. Submission.frt_vgm_tba_plane_closedBall_hausdorff N n T r (applicable as r ≥ 0). unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1) < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top), and ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n < ∞, so μ(B_r(0)) < ∞. Taking real parts (ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_pow, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal with r ≥ 0): μ.real(B_r(0)) = (μ(B_r(0))).toReal = ω_n r^n.

2. Cut-off facts. Let a ∈ ℝ and y ∈ ℝ^N. (i) 0 ≤ χ_a(y) ≤ 1 (outer max with 0, inner min with 1). (ii) If |y| ≥ a, then (a − |y|)/κ ≤ 0 because κ > 0, so min(1, (a − |y|)/κ) ≤ 0 and χ_a(y) = 0. (iii) If |y| ≤ a − κ, then a − |y| ≥ κ, so (a − |y|)/κ ≥ 1, min(1, ·) = 1 and χ_a(y) = 1. (iv) χ_a is continuous (norm, affine maps, division by the constant κ, min and max).

3. Integrability. Let a ≤ 2. χ_a is continuous, hence AE-strongly measurable; |χ_a| ≤ 1 by 2(i); and if y ∉ B_2(0) then |y| > 2 ≥ a, so χ_a(y) = 0 by 2(ii). Since μ(B_2(0)) < ∞ by 1, χ_a is integrable on B_2(0) (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded with bound 1), hence μ-integrable because it vanishes off B_2(0) (IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero). This applies to χ⁻ = χ_1 and to χ⁺ = χ_{1+κ} (1 + κ < 2 since κ < 1). For r ≥ 0 the indicator 1_{B_r(0)} is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff for the Borel set B_r(0), and integrableOn_const using μ(B_r(0)) < ∞ from 1).

4. Lower bound. Pointwise 1_{B_{1−κ}(0)} ≤ χ⁻: if |y| ≤ 1 − κ, then χ⁻(y) = χ_1(y) = 1 by 2(iii) with a = 1; otherwise the indicator is 0 ≤ χ⁻(y) by 2(i). By integral_mono (both sides integrable by 3), ∫ 1_{B_{1−κ}(0)} dμ ≤ ∫ χ⁻ dμ, and ∫ 1_{B_{1−κ}(0)} dμ = μ.real(B_{1−κ}(0)) (integral_indicator_one) = ω_n(1 − κ)^n by 1 with r = 1 − κ ≥ 0 (as κ < 1). This is the first conjunct: ω_n(1 − κ)^n ≤ ∫_{T.plane} χ⁻ dH^n.

5. Upper bound. Pointwise χ⁺ ≤ 1_{B_{1+κ}(0)}: if |y| ≤ 1 + κ, then χ⁺(y) ≤ 1 = 1_{B_{1+κ}(0)}(y) by 2(i); otherwise |y| > 1 + κ and χ⁺(y) = χ_{1+κ}(y) = 0 = 1_{B_{1+κ}(0)}(y) by 2(ii) with a = 1 + κ. By integral_mono (integrability from 3) and integral_indicator_one, ∫ χ⁺ dμ ≤ μ.real(B_{1+κ}(0)) = ω_n(1 + κ)^n by 1 with r = 1 + κ ≥ 0. This is the second conjunct: ∫_{T.plane} χ⁺ dH^n ≤ ω_n(1 + κ)^n. ∎
proof_key_steps: For r ≥ 0, (μHE[n]⌞T.plane)(B_r(0)) = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(r)^n < ∞ (Measure.restrict_apply and sibling plane_ball = Submission.frt_vgm_tba_plane_closedBall_hausdorff), with real value ω_n r^n
Cut-off facts for χ_a(y) = max(0, min(1, (a − |y|)/κ)): 0 ≤ χ_a ≤ 1, χ_a = 0 where |y| ≥ a, χ_a = 1 where |y| ≤ a − κ
χ⁻, χ⁺ and ball indicators are integrable for μHE[n]⌞T.plane (bounded, vanishing off B_2(0) of finite measure)
1_{B_{1−κ}(0)} ≤ χ⁻, integral_mono and integral_indicator_one: ω_n(1−κ)^n ≤ ∫_{T.plane} χ⁻ dH^n

subproblems.title: Def. 1.1 tested on product functions: t^{-n}∫ g(t⁻¹(y−x))β(S) dV → θ β(T) ∫_T g dH^n
subproblems.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N (V : Varifold N n U), x ∈ ℝ^N, T ∈ G(N,n) and θ ∈ ℝ, and suppose HasTangentPlane V x T θ (Simon Ch. 8, Def. 1.1: x ∈ U, θ > 0, and ∫ f dV_{x,t} → θ ∫ f dv(T) as t ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G(N,n)), where V_{x,t} = rescaledMeasure V x t and v(T) = planeVarifoldMeasure T). Then for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) and every continuous β : G(N,n) → ℝ, t^{-n} ∫ g(t⁻¹(y − x)) β(S) dV(y,S) → θ · (β(T) · ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n) as t → 0⁺, where t^{-n} = (t⁻¹)^n, H^n = μHE[n], and all integrals are Bochner integrals (the first with respect to V.measure).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ → ∀ (g : C_c(Euclidean N, ℝ)) (β : C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ)), Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ t⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ z, g (t⁻¹ • (z.1 - x)) * β z.2 ∂V.measure) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (θ * (β T * ∫ y in (T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), g y ∂μHE[n])))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 3–4 of the parent proof (the cut-off test functions and both sides of Def. 1.1). There the function χ_{a,b} is only used through its continuity and compact support, so the same argument is carried out for an arbitrary g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ).

Notation: G := Grassmannian N n; points of ℝ^N × G are z = (z.1, z.2).

1. The test function. Let f(z) := g(z.1) β(z.2). f is continuous (g and β are continuous, and so are the projections). If z ∉ tsupport g × G, then z.1 ∉ tsupport g, so g(z.1) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and f(z) = 0. tsupport g is compact because g has compact support, and G is compact (Grassmannian.instCompactSpace), so tsupport g × G is compact (IsCompact.prod). Hence f has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro), and f is an element of C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ).

2. Def. 1.1 applied to f. The third clause of HasTangentPlane V x T θ, applied to f, gives ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t) → θ · ∫ f d(planeVarifoldMeasure T) as t → 0⁺ (along 𝓝[>] 0).

3. The plane side. By definition planeVarifoldMeasure T = (μHE[n] ⌞ T.plane).map(y ↦ (y, T)). The map y ↦ (y, T) is continuous, hence measurable, and f is continuous, hence AE-strongly measurable, so by integral_map ∫ f d(planeVarifoldMeasure T) = ∫_{T.plane} f(y, T) dH^n(y) = ∫_{T.plane} g(y) β(T) dH^n(y). Pulling out the constant factor (integral_mul_const), this is (∫_{T.plane} g dH^n) · β(T) = β(T) · ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n. So the limit in 2 equals θ · (β(T) · ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n).

4. The rescaled side. Fix t > 0. By definition rescaledMeasure V x t = ENNReal.ofReal(t⁻¹^n) • V.measure.map φ_t with φ_t(z) := (t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x), z.2); φ_t is continuous, hence measurable. By integral_smul_measure, ∫ f d(c • m) = c.toReal · ∫ f dm, and (ENNReal.ofReal(t⁻¹^n)).toReal = t⁻¹^n because t⁻¹^n ≥ 0 (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal). By integral_map (φ_t measurable, f AE-strongly measurable), ∫ f d(V.measure.map φ_t) = ∫ f(φ_t z) dV(z) = ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x)) β(z.2) dV(z). Hence, for every t > 0,
 ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t) = t⁻¹^n · ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x)) β(z.2) dV(z).
No integrability hypothesis is needed: integral_smul_measure holds unconditionally and integral_map only needs the measurability just stated.

5. Conclusion. The functions t ↦ ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t) and t ↦ t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x)) β(z.2) dV(z) agree on (0, ∞), which belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). By Tendsto.congr' and steps 2–3, t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x)) β(z.2) dV(z) → θ · (β(T) · ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n) as t → 0⁺. ∎
proof_key_steps: f(y,S) := g(y)β(S) is continuous and vanishes off the compact set tsupport g × G(N,n), so f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G(N,n))
HasTangentPlane applied to f: ∫ f dV_{x,t} → θ ∫ f dv(T) as t → 0⁺
integral_map along y ↦ (y,T) and integral_mul_const: ∫ f dv(T) = β(T) ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n
for t > 0, integral_smul_measure, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal and integral_map along φ_t: ∫ f dV_{x,t} = t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹(y−x))β(S) dV
the two expressions agree on (0,∞) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0, so Tendsto.congr' transfers the limit

subproblems.title: Cut-off sandwich: ∫ χ_{1−κ,1}(t⁻¹(y−x))β dV ≤ ∫_{Gₙ(B_t(x))} β dV ≤ ∫ χ_{1,1+κ}(t⁻¹(y−x))β dV
subproblems.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N (V : Varifold N n U), x ∈ ℝ^N, β : G(N,n) → ℝ continuous with β ≥ 0, and κ, t ∈ ℝ with 0 < κ < 1, t > 0 and B_{2t}(x) ⊆ U, where B_r(x) = closedBall x r denotes the closed ball. For w ∈ ℝ^N let χ⁻(w) = max(0, min(1, (1 − |w|)/κ)) and χ⁺(w) = max(0, min(1, (1 + κ − |w|)/κ)). Then ∫ χ⁻(t⁻¹(y − x)) β(S) dV(y,S) ≤ ∫_{B_t(x) × G(N,n)} β(S) dV(y,S) ≤ ∫ χ⁺(t⁻¹(y − x)) β(S) dV(y,S), all integrals being Bochner integrals with respect to V.measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (β : C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ)) (κ t : ℝ), 0 < κ → κ < 1 → 0 < t → closedBall x (2 * t) ⊆ U → (∀ S, 0 ≤ β S) → (∫ z, max 0 (min 1 ((1 - ‖t⁻¹ • (z.1 - x)‖) / κ)) * β z.2 ∂V.measure) ≤ ∫ z in closedBall x t ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), β z.2 ∂V.measure ∧ ∫ z in closedBall x t ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), β z.2 ∂V.measure ≤ ∫ z, max 0 (min 1 ((1 + κ - ‖t⁻¹ • (z.1 - x)‖) / κ)) * β z.2 ∂V.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 (local finiteness) and the first half of Step 7 (the pointwise squeeze and its integration) of the parent proof. The positive factor t^{-n} of the parent's I and J is omitted here; it is multiplied in by the consumer.

Notation: G := Grassmannian N n; for z = (z.1, z.2) ∈ ℝ^N × G put w(z) := t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x). B := B_t(x) × G and K := B_{2t}(x) × G, with B_r(x) = closedBall x r. For a ∈ ℝ and w ∈ ℝ^N let χ_a(w) := max(0, min(1, (a − |w|)/κ)); thus χ⁻ = χ_1 and χ⁺ = χ_{1+κ}. Put h⁻(z) := χ⁻(w(z)) β(z.2), h⁺(z) := χ⁺(w(z)) β(z.2) and h(z) := 1_B(z) β(z.2).

1. Finiteness. B_{2t}(x) is compact (closed and bounded in ℝ^N) and B_{2t}(x) ⊆ U by hypothesis, so V(K) = V.measure(B_{2t}(x) × G) < ∞ (V.finite_on_compact). B is Borel (a closed ball times univ), and B ⊆ K since t ≤ 2t.

2. Bound for β. G is compact, so β is bounded: |β(S)| ≤ ‖β‖ for all S, where ‖β‖ is the sup norm (ContinuousMap.norm_coe_le_norm).

3. Geometry. Since t > 0, |w(z)| = t⁻¹ |z.1 − x| = dist(z.1, x)/t (norm_smul). Hence z ∈ B ⇔ dist(z.1, x) ≤ t ⇔ |w(z)| ≤ 1, and z ∉ K ⇒ dist(z.1, x) > 2t ⇒ |w(z)| > 2.

4. Cut-off facts. For all a ∈ ℝ and w ∈ ℝ^N: (i) 0 ≤ χ_a(w) ≤ 1; (ii) if |w| ≥ a, then (a − |w|)/κ ≤ 0 (κ > 0), so χ_a(w) = 0; (iii) if |w| ≤ a − κ, then (a − |w|)/κ ≥ 1, so χ_a(w) = 1.

5. Integrability. Claim: every AE-strongly measurable k : ℝ^N × G → ℝ with |k(z)| ≤ ‖β‖ for all z and k(z) = 0 for all z ∉ K is V.measure-integrable. Indeed k is integrable on K because V(K) < ∞ and k is bounded (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded), and it vanishes off K (IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero). Apply the claim to:
 (a) h⁻: it is continuous; |h⁻(z)| = χ⁻(w(z)) |β(z.2)| ≤ 1 · ‖β‖ by 4(i) and 2; if z ∉ K then |w(z)| > 2 ≥ 1 by 3, so χ⁻(w(z)) = 0 by 4(ii) with a = 1, hence h⁻(z) = 0.
 (b) h⁺: it is continuous; |h⁺| ≤ ‖β‖ likewise; if z ∉ K then |w(z)| > 2 > 1 + κ (as κ < 1), so χ⁺(w(z)) = 0 by 4(ii) with a = 1 + κ, hence h⁺(z) = 0.
 (c) h: it is AE-strongly measurable (indicator of the Borel set B applied to the continuous function z ↦ β(z.2)); |h(z)| ≤ |β(z.2)| ≤ ‖β‖; and h = 0 off B, hence off K.

6. Pointwise sandwich h⁻ ≤ h ≤ h⁺. Let z ∈ ℝ^N × G.
 If z ∈ B: h(z) = β(z.2). Since χ⁻(w(z)) ≤ 1 and β(z.2) ≥ 0, h⁻(z) ≤ β(z.2). By 3, |w(z)| ≤ 1 = (1 + κ) − κ, so χ⁺(w(z)) = 1 by 4(iii) with a = 1 + κ, and h⁺(z) = β(z.2).
 If z ∉ B: h(z) = 0. By 3, |w(z)| > 1, so χ⁻(w(z)) = 0 by 4(ii) with a = 1, and h⁻(z) = 0. Also h⁺(z) = χ⁺(w(z)) β(z.2) ≥ 0 by 4(i) and β ≥ 0.

7. Integration. By 5, 6 and integral_mono, ∫ h⁻ dV ≤ ∫ h dV ≤ ∫ h⁺ dV. As B is Borel, ∫ h dV = ∫ 1_B(z) β(z.2) dV(z) = ∫_B β(z.2) dV(z) (integral_indicator). These are exactly the two asserted inequalities. ∎
proof_key_steps: V(B_{2t}(x) × G) < ∞ by finite_on_compact; |β| ≤ ‖β‖ on the compact Grassmannian
|t⁻¹(y−x)| = |y−x|/t: (y,S) ∈ B_t(x)×G iff |t⁻¹(y−x)| ≤ 1, and |t⁻¹(y−x)| > 2 outside B_{2t}(x)×G
cut-off facts: 0 ≤ χ_a ≤ 1, χ_a(w) = 0 for |w| ≥ a, χ_a(w) = 1 for |w| ≤ a − κ
χ⁻(w)β, χ⁺(w)β and 1_B β are bounded, measurable and vanish off B_{2t}(x)×G, hence V-integrable
pointwise χ⁻(w)β ≤ 1_B β ≤ χ⁺(w)β using β ≥ 0; integral_mono and integral_indicator

subproblems.title: Blow-up limit of ball integrals for β ≥ 0: t^{-n}∫_{Gₙ(B_t(x))} β dV → θ ω_n β(T)
subproblems.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N (V : Varifold N n U), x ∈ ℝ^N, T ∈ G(N,n) and θ ∈ ℝ, and suppose HasTangentPlane V x T θ (Simon Ch. 8, Def. 1.1: x ∈ U, θ > 0, and ∫ f dV_{x,t} → θ ∫ f dv(T) as t ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G(N,n)), where V_{x,t} = rescaledMeasure V x t and v(T) = planeVarifoldMeasure T). Then for every continuous β : G(N,n) → ℝ with β ≥ 0, t^{-n} ∫_{B_t(x) × G(N,n)} β(S) dV(y,S) → θ ω_n β(T) as t → 0⁺, where t^{-n} = (t⁻¹)^n, B_t(x) is the closed ball, ω_n = (unitBallVolume n).toReal, and the integral is the Bochner set integral with respect to V.measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ → ∀ β : C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ), (∀ S, 0 ≤ β S) → Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ t⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ z in closedBall x t ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), β z.2 ∂V.measure) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (θ * (unitBallVolume n).toReal * β T))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 2, 3 and 7 (squeeze for β ≥ 0) of the parent proof. Its three ingredients are supplied by siblings: the blow-up limit for product test functions g(y)β(S) (product_blowup), the pointwise cut-off squeeze integrated against V (ball_cutoff_sandwich), and the bounds for the plane integrals of the cut-offs (plane_cutoff_bounds).

Notation: G := Grassmannian N n; ω := (unitBallVolume n).toReal ≥ 0; J(t) := t⁻¹^n ∫_{B_t(x)×G} β(z.2) dV(z); c := θ β(T) ω. Since θ > 0 (second clause of HasTangentPlane) and β(T) ≥ 0, θβ(T) ≥ 0 and c ≥ 0. The asserted limit θ ω β(T) equals c, so we must show J(t) → c as t → 0⁺.

1. Local finiteness (parent Step 2). By the first clause of HasTangentPlane, x ∈ U, and U is open (V.isOpen_domain), so there is δ > 0 with ball x δ ⊆ U (Metric.isOpen_iff). For 0 < t < δ/2 we have 2t < δ, so B_{2t}(x) ⊆ ball x δ ⊆ U (closedBall_subset_ball). Since (0, δ/2) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0: eventually as t → 0⁺, t > 0 and B_{2t}(x) ⊆ U.

2. Cut-offs in C_c (parent Step 3). Let κ > 0 and a ∈ ℝ, and χ_a(y) := max(0, min(1, (a − |y|)/κ)) for y ∈ ℝ^N. χ_a is continuous, and it vanishes outside the compact ball B_a(0): if |y| > a then (a − |y|)/κ < 0, so the min is < 0 and the max is 0. By HasCompactSupport.intro (with isCompact_closedBall), χ_a has compact support, so it defines g_{a,κ} ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) with g_{a,κ}(y) = χ_a(y) for all y (definitionally). We use g⁻ := g_{1,κ}, i.e. χ⁻(y) = max(0, min(1, (1 − |y|)/κ)), and g⁺ := g_{1+κ,κ}, i.e. χ⁺(y) = max(0, min(1, (1 + κ − |y|)/κ)). These are exactly the cut-offs appearing in the siblings ball_cutoff_sandwich and plane_cutoff_bounds.

3. Reduction. By tendsto_order it suffices to prove: (L) for every a' < c, eventually a' < J(t); and (U) for every b' > c, eventually J(t) < b' (both as t → 0⁺).

4. Proof of (L). Let a' < c and ε := c − a' > 0. The map κ ↦ c(1 − κ)^n is continuous, with value c at κ = 0, and c − ε/2 < c; so eventually as κ → 0⁺, c(1 − κ)^n > c − ε/2. Also eventually 0 < κ < 1. As 𝓝[>] 0 is a nontrivial filter, we can fix κ with 0 < κ < 1 and c(1 − κ)^n > c − ε/2.
 (a) By the sibling product_blowup applied to g⁻ and β: I⁻(t) := t⁻¹^n ∫ χ⁻(t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x)) β(z.2) dV(z) → θ(β(T) c⁻) as t → 0⁺, where c⁻ := ∫_{T.plane} χ⁻ dH^n (H^n = μHE[n]); here g⁻(t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x)) = χ⁻(t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x)) and ∫_{T.plane} g⁻ dH^n = c⁻ by definition of g⁻.
 (b) By the first conjunct of the sibling plane_cutoff_bounds (0 < κ < 1), ω(1 − κ)^n ≤ c⁻. Multiplying by θβ(T) ≥ 0: c(1 − κ)^n = θβ(T)(ω(1 − κ)^n) ≤ θβ(T)c⁻ = θ(β(T)c⁻).
 (c) Since θ(β(T)c⁻) − ε/2 < θ(β(T)c⁻), (a) gives: eventually I⁻(t) > θ(β(T)c⁻) − ε/2 ≥ c(1 − κ)^n − ε/2 > c − ε = a'.
 (d) Eventually (by 1) t > 0 and B_{2t}(x) ⊆ U; then the first conjunct of the sibling ball_cutoff_sandwich (with this κ ∈ (0,1), this t and β ≥ 0) gives ∫ χ⁻(t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x)) β(z.2) dV ≤ ∫_{B_t(x)×G} β(z.2) dV, and multiplying by t⁻¹^n ≥ 0 gives I⁻(t) ≤ J(t).
 Intersecting the two eventual events of (c) and (d): eventually a' < I⁻(t) ≤ J(t).

5. Proof of (U). Let b' > c and ε := b' − c > 0. The map κ ↦ c(1 + κ)^n is continuous with value c at κ = 0, and c < c + ε/2; so eventually as κ → 0⁺, c(1 + κ)^n < c + ε/2, and also eventually 0 < κ < 1. As 𝓝[>] 0 is nontrivial, fix κ with 0 < κ < 1 and c(1 + κ)^n < c + ε/2.
 (a) product_blowup applied to g⁺ and β: I⁺(t) := t⁻¹^n ∫ χ⁺(t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x)) β(z.2) dV(z) → θ(β(T)c⁺), where c⁺ := ∫_{T.plane} χ⁺ dH^n.
 (b) The second conjunct of plane_cutoff_bounds gives c⁺ ≤ ω(1 + κ)^n, so θ(β(T)c⁺) = θβ(T)c⁺ ≤ θβ(T)ω(1 + κ)^n = c(1 + κ)^n.
 (c) Eventually I⁺(t) < θ(β(T)c⁺) + ε/2 ≤ c(1 + κ)^n + ε/2 < c + ε = b'.
 (d) Eventually t > 0, B_{2t}(x) ⊆ U, and the second conjunct of ball_cutoff_sandwich times t⁻¹^n ≥ 0 gives J(t) ≤ I⁺(t).
 Hence eventually J(t) ≤ I⁺(t) < b'.

6. By 3–5, J(t) → c = θ ω β(T) as t → 0⁺, which is the claim (θ ω β(T) = θ β(T) ω by commutativity). ∎
proof_key_steps: x ∈ U open gives δ > 0 with ball x δ ⊆ U, so eventually t > 0 and B_{2t}(x) ⊆ U
the radial cut-offs χ⁻ = max(0,min(1,(1−|y|)/κ)) and χ⁺ = max(0,min(1,(1+κ−|y|)/κ)) are elements of C_c(ℝ^N)

tendsto_order: for a' < θβ(T)ω put ε := θβ(T)ω − a' and pick κ ∈ (0,1) with θβ(T)ω(1−κ)^n > a' + ε/2; product_blowup and plane_cutoff_bounds bound I⁻(t) from below eventually; ball_cutoff_sandwich gives I⁻(t) ≤ J(t)

symmetrically for b' > θβ(T)ω put ε := b' − θβ(T)ω and pick κ ∈ (0,1) with θβ(T)ω(1+κ)^n < b' − ε/2; product_blowup with χ⁺ and plane_cutoff_bounds bound I⁺(t) from above eventually; ball_cutoff_sandwich gives J(t) ≤ I⁺(t)
hence t⁻¹^n ∫_{B_t(x)×G} β dV → θ ω_n β(T)
